title: Finite generation of bounded finite-model constructible complexes by strata
statement: Let $\Lambda$ be a commutative condensed ring [sk-def-sfb-condensed-ring]. For every scheme $T$, put $B_T=p_T^*\Lambda$ [sk-def-sfb-pulled-back-coefficients], and use the ordinary uncompleted category $D(B_T)=D(\operatorname{Mod}_{B_T})$ [sk-def-sfb-derived-categories]. Let $X$ be a scheme with Noetherian underlying topological space (descending chains of closed subsets stabilize). Let $\mathscr C$ be an isomorphism-closed class of objects of $D(B_X)$ containing zero, closed under all integer shifts and under extensions: if $A\to B\to C\to A[1]$ is distinguished and $A,C\in\mathscr C$, then $B\in\mathscr C$ [def-weil-triangulated-category]. Suppose $v_!t_*L[0]\in\mathscr C$ for every open immersion $v:V\hookrightarrow X$, every reduced closed immersion $t:S\hookrightarrow V$, and every $B_S$-module sheaf $L$ with a finite constant local model [def-sfb-module-open-lower-shriek, def-sfb-module-lower-star, def-weil-open-immersion, def-weil-closed-immersion, def-pc-reduced-scheme, sk-def-sfb-constructible]. Then every $K\in D(B_X)$ with bounded constructible cohomology in the finite constant local model sense of [sk-def-sfb-constructible] lies in $\mathscr C$. Only finitely many extensions and shifts are needed for each $K$. The assertion includes arbitrary condensed coefficients and integral torsion local models.

source.place: Tag 08J5 (remark-truncation-distinguished-triangle); finite-stratum refinement is Stacks topology Tag 09Y5 (lemma-noetherian-partition-refined-by-stratification). Agent extraction of Bhatt–Scholze Proposition 6.8.11(3) and Lemma 6.3.14.

proof.text: First let $F$ be any constructible $B_X$-module sheaf in the finite constant local model sense. Apply [lem-sfb-finite-model-stratum-filtration], which assumes exactly a topologically Noetherian scheme and arbitrary commutative condensed coefficients. It supplies a finite filtration $0=F_0\subset F_1\subset\cdots\subset F_r=F$ and isomorphisms $Q_k:=F_k/F_{k-1}\cong v_{k!}(t_k)_*L_k$. Here $v_k:V_k\hookrightarrow X$ is open, $t_k:S_k\hookrightarrow V_k$ is reduced closed, and $L_k$ has a finite constant local model. These are precisely generators allowed by the hypothesis, so $Q_k[0]\in\mathscr C$ by isomorphism closure. All the localization and refinement assertions used here are conclusions of the cited filtration statement; no local freeness or finite Tor amplitude is imposed.

source.place: Tag 09Y5 (lemma-noetherian-partition-refined-by-stratification), in the sheaf formulation of lem-sfb-finite-model-stratum-filtration

proof.text: For each $1\le k\le r$, put the short exact sequence $0\to F_{k-1}\to F_k\to Q_k\to0$ in degree zero. It is degreewise short exact: it is the displayed sheaf sequence in degree zero and the zero sequence in every other degree. By [lem-weil-pbc-complex-ses-triangle] it gives a distinguished triangle $F_{k-1}[0]\to F_k[0]\to Q_k[0]\to F_{k-1}[1]$. Induct on $k$: the initial object $F_0[0]=0$ lies in $\mathscr C$; if $F_{k-1}[0]$ lies in it, then $Q_k[0]$ from step 1 and extension closure put the middle term $F_k[0]$ in it. Thus $F[0]\in\mathscr C$ after at most $r$ extensions. For $r=0$ this is just the zero-object hypothesis.

source.place: Tag 0152 (lemma-derived-canonical-delta-functor), applied to sheaves concentrated in degree zero

proof.text: Now take the given $K$, choose a cochain representative, and choose integers $a\le b$ such that $H^q(K)=0$ outside $[a,b]$. Write $T_q=\tau_{\le q}K$. By [lem-weil-pbc-truncation-cohomology], $H^i(T_q)\cong H^i(K)$ for $i\le q$ and is zero for $i>q$. In particular $T_{a-1}$ is acyclic. The map $0\to T_{a-1}$ is therefore a quasi-isomorphism, hence an isomorphism in the localization defining the derived category [def-weil-abstract-derived-category]. Thus $T_{a-1}\in\mathscr C$. Likewise $T_b\to K$ induces isomorphisms on cohomology for $i\le b$; for $i>b$ both sides have zero cohomology. It too is a quasi-isomorphism, so $T_b\cong K$. These are direct uses of the cohomology formula and the definition of a quasi-isomorphism, not convergence of an infinite truncation tower.

source.place: Tag 0118 (section-truncations), canonical upper truncations; localization at quasi-isomorphisms as in Tag 05RU (definition-derived-category)

proof.text: Induct on the finite list $q=a,a+1,\ldots,b$, starting with $T_{a-1}\in\mathscr C$ from step 3. By [lem-weil-pbc-truncation-triangle], the successive cohomology triangle is $T_{q-1}\to T_q\to H^q(K)[-q]\to T_{q-1}[1]$. Each $H^q(K)$ is constructible by the hypothesis on $K$, so steps 1 and 2 give $H^q(K)[0]\in\mathscr C$, and closure under the integer shift $[-q]$ gives $H^q(K)[-q]\in\mathscr C$. If $T_{q-1}\in\mathscr C$, extension closure in this triangle gives $T_q\in\mathscr C$. At $q=b$ obtain $T_b\in\mathscr C$; the isomorphism $T_b\cong K$ from step 3 and isomorphism closure give $K\in\mathscr C$. Only existence of the stated distinguished triangle is used, not any uniqueness or functoriality clause.

source.place: Tag 08J5 (remark-truncation-distinguished-triangle), successive cohomology triangles with a=q-1

proof.text: For each of the finitely many $q\in[a,b]$, let $r_q$ be the finite length of the filtration chosen in step 1 for $H^q(K)$. The construction uses at most $\sum_{q=a}^b r_q+(b-a+1)$ extensions and at most $b-a+1$ shifts of the resulting sheaves. The sum is finite. If $K$ is acyclic, one can instead use the quasi-isomorphism $0\to K$ and no extensions. The empty scheme is included because the filtration theorem permits length zero. No step uses a coefficient-field argument, a resolution by finite free modules, or inversion of torsion; hence the same construction applies to every commutative condensed ring and to integral torsion local models.
